decisive_items: He had undergone bariatric surgery 10 years prior
Shows constriction of the junction of gastric fundus and body
increased annular density shadow in front of the ilium in right lower abdomen
response.rationale: Prior bariatric surgery with proximal obstruction and right-lower-quadrant annular/constrictive findings most specifically indicates an internal hernia; the free gas and pneumatosis are best read as secondary strangulation/perforation rather than the primary diagnosis.

rejected.why: Free gas and pneumatosis are complications but do not explain the bariatric-related constriction, annular density, or proximal bowel dilation.
No tract or extravasation is shown; free gas/pneumatosis are nonspecific and vomiting bile does not establish a fistula.
Intestinal obstruction is a broader syndrome that is consistent, but it underspecifies the post-bariatric internal hernia mechanism suggested by the upper GI findings.
Thickened wall, rebound, and high CRP can accompany strangulation/ischemia, but there is no primary vascular/ischemic pattern and the bariatric surgical evidence favors internal hernia as the cause.
